name: TROPONIN I
description: Troponin I measures cardiac muscle injury and is the gold standard for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction. This high-sensitivity test detects myocardial damage with excellent specificity.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Troponin I is a cardiac-specific protein released from damaged myocardial cells. High sensitivity troponin I is the preferred biomarker for acute myocardial infarction diagnosis. Normal <0.04 ng/mL (99th percentile). Levels rise 3-6 hours after myocardial injury, peak at 12-24 hours, and remain elevated for 7-10 days. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides excellent sensitivity and specificity. Used in chest pain evaluation, AMI diagnosis, and risk stratification. Serial measurements (0, 3, 6 hours) improve diagnostic accuracy. Also elevated in myocarditis, cardiac contusion, and cardiotoxic chemotherapy. Critical for rapid rule-out/rule-in of myocardial infarction in emergency settings.
